about: Verified facts about game data and memory, with their status PER GAME and a check that re-runs them. A finding verified on one game is a hypothesis on the other: run verify_finding there and record the result here (status, date, where, evidence). Statuses: verified | differs | unverified | n/a. Check kinds: data (game_data: row n of a game data table contains the expected text - the cheapest cross-game check), correlate (memory_correlate finds a bit equal to `expect` with 0 counterexamples), stored (the label's value is stored in the range), eval (eval_path value matches `expect`), code (find_field_access: a decompiled excerpt of the struct's code contains every `expectAll` string - needs Ghidra and a snapshot of that game's exe), series (observe_series over the observer journal: `unit` holds `expect.relation` - same value, same step or step xK - with `expect.unit`; needs observation on long enough), script (`code`, C# run in the HUD through run_csharp, returns {verdict: pass|differs|fail|not now, where, evidence}; needs Allow C# Scripts), manual (an experiment: follow `how`).

findings.title: ServerData +0x7100 mirrors +0x6500 (0xC00 apart; also 0x7700/0x6B00, 0x6DA0/0x61A0, 0x7080/0x6480): a double-buffered copy

poe2.evidence: observe_series layer=server unit=0x7100 (town, ~10 min over several HUD runs): 0x6500 same value in 152/152 paired changes, 258/258 changes within 200 ms of each other. findings.title: Stash tab +60 = a 1-byte Map stash setting (unmapped by the HUD), present when Flags bit 4 is set; not a folder field
findings.subject: ServerStashTab

poe1.evidence: find_field_access: (de)serializer reads or writes 1 byte at +0x3C only if (flags & 0x10). The Edit Stash Tab apply handler FUN_14025b420 diffs old/new tab descriptors (FUN_140256270: 1 name, 2 colour, 4 Flags bit 3 checkbox, 8 this byte, 0x10 guild permissions, 0x20 folder/parent, 0x40 affinities) and applies change 8 only when TabType == 5 (MapStash): it writes the byte to the tab, copies it to every child page (Flags bit 5, +58 == the tab) and sends packet 0xD0 {tab index, byte, stash kind}. 0 with bit 4 clear on all 80 player and 21 guild tabs, including 2 new folders (TabType 16), so folders don't use it. What the Map stash setting is, is unknown (the dialog itself carries it unchanged). Ruled out by experiment map-stash-0x3c (queued, user-run): the Maps tab Edit dialog has no Map-only option; changing colour and setting the Map affinity, then the colour back, changed +44, +61 bit 6 and +63 but never +60. The Map stash panel has no view or filter option (only tier buttons and numbered pages), and tier and page clicks in earlier runs never set bit 4. Likely set by the server or a feature not visible in this league; it is not a user setting

findings.title: HUD bug: GetClientRect() of elements inside IngameUi.WorldMap[0] (the pan container) is off horizontally by pan.X x (W/2560 - H/1600): the HUD scales the pan by H/1600, the game by W/2560
findings.subject: Element.GetClientRect under IngameUi.WorldMap (waypoint Teleport and caravan Travel maps)

poe1.note: PoE1's HUD uses the same x scale (Camera.Width / 2560 / (aspect / 1.6) = Height / 1600); whether the PoE1 game pans its world map by W/2560 is unmeasured. The bridge's highlight correction is off on PoE1 (WorldMapPanCorrected) until it is

poe2.where: 1920x1080: 0.075 px per layout unit of WorldMap[0].Position.X (pan clamps at +-422.4 on the Act 2 map: +-31.7 px)
poe2.evidence: Whats A Route: pan.X -2.9 -> HUD x 883.7 vs orb ~881; pan.X -340.8 -> HUD 766.9 vs orb ~740 (27 px = 340.8 x 0.079). Bridge highlights (guided drags with the user, Teleport view): at pan -422.4 the raw box was 32-35 px right of the icon, corrected ~2 px; at +422.4 raw 31.7 px left, corrected ~1-2 px. Vertical is exact. Node offsets inside the container are right; only the pan is under-scaled. Read the pan raw from WorldMap[0] +0x100 (finding ui.worldmap.pan-offset): WorldMap[0].Position and the rects built from it are cached and trail a drag (9.4 px avg, 52 px max)

check.how: Open the waypoint (Teleport) or caravan Travel map and drag it far sideways. The script checks the HUD side (rect.X = (pan + node offsets) x H/1600); the game side (it pans by W/2560) needs a screenshot: tools\screenshot.ps1 next to a highlighted node, box vs icon ~ pan.X x (W/2560 - H/1600) apart.
code: var wm = GameController.IngameState.IngameUi.WorldMap;
var cam = GameController.IngameState.Camera;
float sy = cam.Height / 1600f, sx = cam.Width / 2560f;
var c0 = wm != null && wm.Address != 0 && wm.IsVisible && wm.ChildCount > 0 ? wm.GetChildAtIndex(0) : null;
Element node = null;
if (c0 != null) { var q = new Queue<Element>(); q.Enqueue(c0); var n = 0;
while (q.Count > 0 && n++ < 400 && node == null) { var e = q.Dequeue();
for (var i = 0; i < e.ChildCount && node == null; i++) { var c = e.GetChildAtIndex(i); if (c == null || !c.IsVisible) continue;
var cr = c.GetClientRect(); if (cr.Width > 10 && cr.Width < 120) node = c; else q.Enqueue(c); } } }
float pan = c0?.Position.X ?? 0, below = 0;
for (var p = node; p != null && p.Address != c0.Address; p = p.Parent) below += p.Position.X;
var r = node?.GetClientRect();
var wmX = wm?.GetClientRect().X ?? 0;
var byHeight = wmX + (pan + below) * sy; var byWidth = wmX + pan * sx + below * sy;
var drift = pan * (sx - sy);
c0 == null ? (object)new { verdict = "not now", evidence = "the world map is closed: open a waypoint (Teleport) or the caravan's Travel map" }
: node == null ? new { verdict = "fail", evidence = $"world map open but no node-sized visible element under WorldMap[0] ({c0.ChildCount} children): its layout changed" }
: Math.Abs(drift) < 5 ? new { verdict = "not now", evidence = $"pan.X {pan:F1} gives only {drift:F1} px drift at {cam.Width}x{cam.Height}: drag the map far sideways (or the screen is 16:10)" }

: Math.Abs(r.Value.X - byHeight) < 1 ? new { verdict = "pass", where = $"{cam.Width}x{cam.Height}, pan.X {pan:F1}", evidence = $"HUD rect.X {r.Value.X:F1} = (pan + node offsets) x H/1600 ({byHeight:F1}); the game pans by W/2560, so the box is {drift:F1} px off (correct by pan.X x (W/2560 - H/1600))" }

: Math.Abs(r.Value.X - byWidth) < 1 ? new { verdict = "differs", where = $"{cam.Width}x{cam.Height}, pan.X {pan:F1}", evidence = $"HUD rect.X {r.Value.X:F1} already scales the pan by W/2560 ({byWidth:F1}): the HUD fixed it, drop the correction" }

: new { verdict = "fail", where = $"{cam.Width}x{cam.Height}, pan.X {pan:F1}", evidence = $"HUD rect.X {r.Value.X:F1} matches neither H/1600 ({byHeight:F1}) nor W/2560 ({byWidth:F1}) pan scaling: the rect formula changed" }

findings.title: The world map's pan (WorldMap[0].Position, layout units) is two floats at WorldMap[0] +0x100; read raw, it is current while the HUD's cached Position trails a drag
findings.subject: IngameUi.WorldMap[0] (pan container element)

poe2.evidence: At rest +0x100/+0x104 = Position exactly (339.7334, 109.62964). Whats A Route: over 667 samples while dragging, the cached Position trailed the raw read by 9.4 px avg, 52 px max. The bridge calibrates it each time the map opens (CalibratePan: hint, else a scan of the first 0x400 bytes) and moves highlight boxes with it every frame; mid-drag screenshots show boxes on their icons

check.how: Open the waypoint (Teleport) or caravan Travel map and leave it still (ideally panned away from 0, 0); the script compares the floats at +0x100 with WorldMap[0].Position and scans 0x400 bytes if they moved.
code: var wm = GameController.IngameState.IngameUi.WorldMap;
var c0 = wm != null && wm.Address != 0 && wm.IsVisible && wm.ChildCount > 0 ? wm.GetChildAtIndex(0) : null;
var m = GameController.Memory;
var p1 = c0?.Position; System.Threading.Thread.Sleep(50); var p2 = c0?.Position;
bool Same(float a, float b) => Math.Abs(a - b) < 0.01f;
var atRest = c0 != null && Same(p1.Value.X, p2.Value.X) && Same(p1.Value.Y, p2.Value.Y);
var hit = c0 != null && Same(m.Read<float>(c0.Address + 0x100), p2.Value.X) && Same(m.Read<float>(c0.Address + 0x104), p2.Value.Y);
int? moved = null;

if (atRest && !hit && (p2.Value.X != 0 || p2.Value.Y != 0)) for (var off = 0; off + 8 <= 0x400 && moved == null; off += 4) if (Same(m.Read<float>(c0.Address + off), p2.Value.X) && Same(m.Read<float>(c0.Address + off + 4), p2.Value.Y)) moved = off;
c0 == null ? (object)new { verdict = "not now", evidence = "the world map is closed: open a waypoint (Teleport) or the caravan's Travel map" }
: !atRest ? new { verdict = "not now", evidence = "the map is moving: let go of it" }
: hit && p2.Value.X == 0 && p2.Value.Y == 0 ? new { verdict = "not now", evidence = "pan is (0, 0), which any zeroed pair matches: drag the map away from its start first" }

: hit ? new { verdict = "pass", where = "WorldMap[0] +0x100 (x), +0x104 (y), float", evidence = $"+0x100 = ({m.Read<float>(c0.Address + 0x100):F2}, {m.Read<float>(c0.Address + 0x104):F2}) = Position ({p2.Value.X:F2}, {p2.Value.Y:F2})" }

: moved != null ? new { verdict = "fail", where = $"WorldMap[0] +0x{moved:X}", evidence = $"moved: Position ({p2.Value.X:F2}, {p2.Value.Y:F2}) is at +0x{moved:X} now, +0x100 reads {m.Read<float>(c0.Address + 0x100):F2}: update the bridge's WorldMapPanOffset hint" }
: new { verdict = "fail", evidence = $"no float pair equal to Position ({p2.Value.X:F2}, {p2.Value.Y:F2}) in WorldMap[0]'s first 0x400 bytes (+0x100 reads {m.Read<float>(c0.Address + 0x100):F2})" }
